question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Attempting to impress by affecting greater importance or merit than is actually possessed
solution:
The correct answer is ***Option 1)***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Pretentious"** means attempting to impress by affecting greater importance or merit than is actually possessed. (दिखावटी)

 
 
• **Example: **His** *pretentious*** manner of speaking made him seem arrogant and insincere.
 
 
 
• **"Imperious" **refers to assuming power or authority without justification; arrogant and domineering. (घमंडी)
 
 
• **Example: **Her ***imperious*** attitude made it difficult for her to make friends.
 
 

Hence, we can infer that the word for 'attempting to impress by affecting greater importance or merit than is actually possessed' is **'Pretentious'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Imperious **(घमंडी): Assuming power or authority without justification; arrogant and domineering.

 
 
• **Example:** Her*** imperious*** attitude made it difficult for her to make friends.
 
 
 
• **Airy **(हवादार ): Giving an impression of being unconcerned or nonchalant.
 
 
• **Example: **He had an*** airy ***disregard for the rules.
 
 
 
• **Glorious** (शानदार): Having, worthy of, or bringing fame or admiration.
 
 
• **Example:** The team had a ***glorious*** victory in the finals.
